text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Failed businessman Alan Bond admitted to taking part in the biggest robbery in Australian history yesterday when he pleaded guilty in the West Australian Supreme Court to two charges relating to the siphoning of more than A$1 billion from Bell Resources. The money was siphoned out of Bell into Bond Corp through back-to-back loans in late 1988 and early 1989. Page 1.

Prime Minister John Howard's announcement yesterday that the Government would call for tenders for a very fast train between Sydney and Canberra was welcomed by the Speedrail group, which has proposed a A$2 billion train backed by a A$200 million investment from international high speed train operator GEC Alsthom. Page 2.

Korea Zinc president Choi Chang-Keun said yesterday that he expects to receive Foreign Investment Review Board approval for a A$1.2 billion zinc smelter in Townsville within the next three weeks. Choi said the smelter would become the world's biggest zinc smelter and possibly the last greenfield project of its type anywhere in the world. Page 5.

Commonwealth Investment Management Services, the asset management arm of the Commonwealth Bank of Australia, and asset consulting firm Towers Perrin have beaten eight other bidders to be named as preferred bidders for the Federal Government's A$9 billion uperannuation funds management business, Commonwealth Funds Management. Page 21.

Coles Myer Ltd chief operating officer Dennis Eck was yesterday "cautiously optimistic" about the retailer's sales over the next month, saying that because of an improvement in sales in the past week Coles did not expect to engage in heavy discounting during the Christmas period. Page 21.

According to market sources in Taipei, BHP is seeking to sell its loss-making BHP Steel Building Products Ltd Taiwan, which has assets estimated at about A$60 million to A$70 million. The sell-off has been sparked by a continuing slump in the Taiwan construction sector, which has also seen BTR Nylex recently announce plans to withdraw from the island. Page 22.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Aggressive selling in the United States has left the Australian dollar revalued, after a turbulent 24 hours which saw the dollar lose up to US3 cents. The dollar's drop followed comments by former Reserve Bank of Australia governor Bernie Fraser that the RBA's recent interest rate cut of half a per cent should have been as high as one per cent. Page 31.

The Federal Court in Melbourne has been told by Qantas Airways Ltd that it will cease trading if the Federal Airports Corp proceeds with a threat to lock the carrier out of five domestic airport terminals around the country next week. The FAC expects Qanas to reach a sub-lease agreement with Aussie Airlines by 5pm next Monday to avoid the threat. Page 31.

Yellow Pages holding company Pacific Access Pty Ltd lifted sales of Telstra's Yellow Pages 5.6 per cent to A$746 million in the 12 months to June. The figures show the fifth consecutive year of the Yellow Pages lifting profits and revenue, yet the benefits to Telstra have been reduced to only five per cent of total revenue. Page 31.

The AIF Telecommunications Fund, a private investment fund backed by some of the world's richest people, including the Sultan of Brunei, George Soros and Li Kashing and an offshoot of the Asian Infrastructure Fund, has entered the Australian market, taking a small stake in the booming mobile phone industry and showing interest in the transport and power industries after deregulation. Page 31.

Commonwealth Investments Services Ltd, a wholly owned subsidiary of the Commonwealth Bank of Australia, was yesterday named by Finance Minister John Fahey as the preferred bidder for the A$8 billion Commonwealth Funds Management Ltd, the superannuation inestment vehicle for Canberra-based public servants. Page 31.

AMP Society, one of Australia's largest financial institutions, will next year ask its shareholders to give approval for a radical drive into international operations that will be fuelled by a A$15 billion listing on the Australian Stock Exchange. Initial plans, including expanding marketing links with the Virgin Group, acquisitions in Europe and the dropping of general insurance, should be approved by the AMP board next week. Page 33.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

As the Australian dollar fell US2.5 cents overnight in both London and New York, reasons for the fall pointed at speculation over further interest rate cuts and the influence of large US hedge funds, possibly led by George Soros's Quantum fund which drove the turbulent trade. Page 25.

As stockbroking analysts suggest the New South Wales Government will need to add a sweetener, such as the State's lotteries, to the estimated A$1 billion float of the NSW TAB to successfully attract institutional investors, State Treasurer Michael Egan sad the Government was yet to make a final decision on the privatisation. Page 25.

As entrepreneur Alan Bond was found guilty of Australia's biggest fraud, he did not let his prospective jail term get in the way of his confidence of eventually reviving his business career. However, Bond is already in prison, serving three year's jail for fraud over the La Promenade painting, and he will face up to five years for each of the charges he pleaded guilty to yesterday. Page 25.

The Commonwealth Bank was yesterday named as the preferred bidder for the Federal Government's A$7 billion Commonwealth Funds Management operation. The successful buyout of CFM by Commonwealth subsidiary Commonwealth Investment Services (CIS) would see CBA jump into fourth place in the big league of fund managers with A$21.5 billion of funds under management. Page 25.

Seven Network chairman Kerry Stokes says he is prepared to discuss the settlement of the legal dispute with Optus Vision, which, if resolved, could allow Optus Communications to go ahead with its planned A$4.5 billion sharemarket listing. Stokes claims he is willing to forgive some Optus shareholders if Seven's point of view is appreciated. Page 27.

According to a survey by Rich Kachor Research, for the first time in years, the volume of net funds trickling into rollover funds has fallen. The survey showed for the year to September 30, net funds being transferred into the super lump sum rollover market fell by nine per cent to A$23 billion. Page 27.
THE AGE

The Australian dollar appears to have made a comeback after falling to 78.55 US cents in New York on Tuesday night. The fall followed comments by former Reserve Bank governor Bernie Fraser that suggested the November 6 interest rate cut could have been higher. Economists and dealers expect the dollar will make a full recovery and may pass Monday's six year high of 82.03 US cents. Page B1.

National Australia Bank will look to buy a controlling stake in the Philippine National Bank subsidiary PNB-Republic Bank, based in Manila. Sixty per cent of the Bank will be auctioned on 18 December at a reserve price of 800 million pesos (A$37.5 millio), and the NAB is one of eight banks to have shown interest in the deal. Page B1.

Currency dealers claimed yesterday Hungarian-born US billionaire George Soros, along with several other US funds, was the seller that ignited the rapid depreciation of the Australian dollar. Soros has made a fortune trading the world's currencies, and has been responsible for some of the largest foreign exchange movements in the past ten years. Page B1.

The Optus Communications 1996 industry development report, released yesterday, showed a 12 per cent-plus growth in telecommunications has generated more than A$15 billion of investment by Optus, Telstra and Vodaphone over the past four years. These figures are well ahead of original forecasts. Page B3.

Perth-based Golden Valley Mines NL and its Indonesian partner PT Krueng Gasui (KG) are still involved in the hunt for a slice of the monster Busang gold deposit in Kalimantan, Indonesia. It is hoped the dispute between KG and Canadian miner Bre-X Mineral, the current owner of Busang, will be resolved soon. Page B3.

American consulting firm Channel Tactics president Bruce Fredrickson yesterday told the National Trade and Investment Outlook Conference that Australian computer software firms must throw themselves into the United States, and the Australian finance indusry must follow. Page B3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
